name: Tomas Walsh

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: I am with the independent Work Futures Panel, with no ties to employers, AI firms, unions, parties or government. Your answers stay confidential; what does your factory day involve?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: I lead a glass-bottle blowing line and check the first neck after a mould change. I have a two-year technical diploma and am one of the best at hearing when the mould sits wrong. I like a bottle that seals cleanly and dislike a chipped neck sent to packing.

opening.speaker: interviewer
opening.text: Who shares the bills, and how do you use AI?

opening.speaker: persona
opening.text: My wife Mari is a dental nurse and our grown children have homes of their own. We have a mortgage, three months of expenses saved, my typical operator pay and some similar glass plants nearby. I use AI now and then to group shift stoppages, but check every batch with a gauge.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: This one is called AI Plateau. Picture this. AI turns out to be mostly hype. It automates some routine tasks and saves a bit of time here and there, but nothing radical changes. Jobs, pay and prices carry on much as they would have anyway. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would tell the glassworks that a little help sorting orders is welcome. The first bottle off the blowing machine still needs its neck checked before the whole run starts.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I lead the bottle line and can hear a misaligned mould before a gauge confirms it. My wife Mari is a dental nurse, our grown children live separately, and our two wages cover the mortgage with three months saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the blowing shift and use my occasional AI notes to group stoppages, then check them against the physical measurements. I would put a little of each new full wage toward the mortgage after bills rather than move money already saved.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would feel calm about small improvements. Mari and I can still walk to the market after my Friday shift without making a new career plan.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What do you check at the neck?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A hairline chip can appear where the cap seals. I reject the first bottle and reset the mould before the packer receives a whole crate.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How often do you use AI?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now and then for shift notes. I trust a calibrated gauge on a bottle more than a tidy paragraph.

I would use **occasional AI notes** beside measured checks.
think: Our **three-month reserve** covers a short interruption.
Mari’s **dental wage** and my typical pay cover the mortgage now.
do: Keep **bottle-blowing shifts** and check first necks.
Compare **AI stoppage notes** with calibrated gauges.
Pay extra **mortgage principal** from new full wages after bills.
feel: **Calm** about present work and household bills.
S0.quote: A hairline chip can appear where the cap seals.
fieldNote: His **technical diploma** and exceptional mould diagnosis support senior leadership on the blowing line.
The **three-month reserve** is existing household money; extra debt payment comes only from future full wages.

steps.text: Keep bottle-blowing shifts and inspect first necks
Pay extra mortgage principal from new full wages after bills

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider Steady Disruption. Now picture this. AI brings strong change, but not a revolution. Over the next few years it takes over many thinking tasks in many jobs: writing, checking, planning, buying, booking, coding and answering customers. Robots spread into hands-on work more slowly. Some jobs shrink, new ones appear, and lots of people have to change how they work. Most people still have work, and there is some time to adjust. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would say the office can automate bookings, but a robot taking hot bottles off a mould needs guarded practice. I will try a new defect chart after the setter has checked it on reject bottles.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: If a robot unloads the machine, the packer’s shift and perhaps some of mine could shrink. Three months saved helps, but the mortgage still needs earned wages and nearby glass plants have only some openings.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would ask for an offered paid practice slot with the conveyor isolated, reject bottles on the bench and the setter present. If approved, I would learn the new AI neck-defect chart against gauge readings; after actual hours cuts, I would apply for posted reachable glass jobs only where pay after travel covers the mortgage and food.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about a possible cut to my hours, but willing to compare a tested chart with a real bottle. The cap does not care which screen liked the neck.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you let a robot grade the first live crate?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Not before an offered paid guarded practice slot and the setter’s sign-off. I would check the first crate by hand too.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would make another job worthwhile?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: An actual posting with weekly hours and enough net pay after travel. A plant name alone cannot pay our mortgage.

I would keep **gauge checks** beside every new alert.

steps.text: Practise only in offered paid guarded isolated-conveyor slot

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2028. Next one. The singularity hits fast. Within 2 years, by 2028, there is full AGI: artificial general intelligence, meaning AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do, as well or better, and cheaper. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2031. It arrives before most companies, governments and families have time to prepare. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AGI in 2028 finds me sixty, and capable bottle-handling robots around 2031 find me sixty-three. The office changes first, while the moulding floor changes when robots can handle hot glass.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I expect the plant to close one bottle shift once robots can unload and inspect the line. My lead post could be in that shift, and Mari’s dental wage with three months saved would not carry the mortgage through a long search; I am awake over that.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would request written shift and severance terms and postpone replacing our kitchen cabinets. If I get a real cut notice, I would apply for posted reachable glass or packing roles with bill-covering net pay after travel and a confirmed start date before leaving; if none appears, I would ask the lender about temporary terms.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be alarmed about a likely large loss of household income. A crate of perfect bottles cannot stand in for a pay packet.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would you retire at sixty-three?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Only if verified retirement income and Mari’s confirmed wage covered housing, food and health costs. I have not seen those numbers.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Could grown children help?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have households of their own. A ride to an interview might help, but their pay is not in our budget.

say: I would seek **written shift terms** before 2031 robots.
I would ask for **severance figures** if a shift closes.
think: A **bottle shift** may close around 2031 after capable robots arrive.
My **lead post** could go too, leaving our mortgage exposed.
do: Request **written staffing and severance** from management.
Postpone **kitchen-cabinet replacement** while shifts are uncertain.
Apply after **cut notice** for posted reachable bill-covering net-pay work.
feel: **Alarmed** and losing sleep over expected major wage loss.
S2.quote: A crate of perfect bottles cannot stand in for a pay packet.
fieldNote: He expects **major shift loss** that may include his lead post, supporting alarm.
Three **months saved** and some nearby plants give search time, but a move needs real adequate pay.
Leave only after a real offer and **confirmed start date**, preserving paid work until then.

steps.text: Request written bottle-line staffing and severance terms
Apply after cut notice for posted reachable bill-covering net-pay glass or packing role
Ask lender for temporary terms if no adequate offer appears

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2031. Now the same thing, a bit slower. Full AGI arrives within 5 years, by 2031: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2034. There are a few years to see it coming, but it's still fast. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AGI in 2031 finds me sixty-three, and capable bottle robots around 2034 find me sixty-six. Five years could give the plant time to train experienced operators in mould maintenance.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I can hear a bad mould, but a maintenance post needs a recognised qualification and supervised safe work. Unpaid course time would cut the mortgage budget, and I want a reachable posted job before changing lanes.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid blowing shift and ask for a funded maintenance course on paid time. If offered an actual place with the mould cooled and isolated, a qualified fitter supervising and a posted reachable role at bill-covering net pay after travel, I would enrol; after qualifying I would apply for that role.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be anxious about later cuts, though I can learn from a proven practical course. A mould can cool before I put my hands on it.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Who would supervise practice?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: A fitter would lock out the machine and show the first mould adjustment on a cold training unit. I would need an offered paid place.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If no place opens?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would keep the paid line while possible and compare posted glass jobs after cuts. I would not buy private classes with our reserve.

say: I would ask for **paid mould-maintenance training** before capable robots change the line.
I would require **posted local wages** that cover the mortgage after travel.
think: My **mould knowledge** helps but is not a maintenance qualification.
An **unpaid course** would strain the mortgage budget.
do: Enrol in **funded maintenance course** only with offered paid safe practice and adequate posted role.
Apply after **qualification** for posted reachable bill-covering net-pay mould work.
feel: **Anxious** about later cuts, open to proved supervised practice.
S3.quote: A mould can cool before I put my hands on it.
fieldNote: His **steady adaptability** supports taught mechanical learning, not assumed qualification.
The **later application** requires offered funded paid safe practice and a posted reachable adequate job.

steps.text: Keep paid bottle-blowing shifts while available
Enrol only with funded fees, paid time, isolated cooled mould and qualified fitter supervising
Require reachable posted mould job covering bills after travel before enrolling; apply once qualified

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Now consider AGI by 2036. Last one. Full AGI arrives within 10 years, by 2036: AI that can do almost any thinking work a person can do. Robots that can do hands-on work as well as people come about 3 years later, around 2039. It's the same end point, but there's about a decade to prepare, change careers and make plans. If this happened, what would you say about it at work, to friends, or online?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Thinking AGI in 2036 finds me sixty-eight, and capable bottle robots around 2039 find me seventy-one. Ten years lets Mari and me see what our mortgage and retirement figures really say.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: And just between us, off the record, what do you really think it means for you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: We had hoped I could stop full-time shifts around sixty-seven, but three months saved will not pay for years outside work. I do not know what any pension would pay or what Mari’s future hours will be.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: What would you actually do, starting now and in the first year after it arrives? Be as specific as you can.

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: Now in 2026 I would keep the blowing shift and pay a little extra mortgage principal from new full wages after bills. I would request retirement and mortgage figures; if verified household income covers housing, food and health costs at sixty-seven I would leave factory work then, otherwise continue safe paid work, and after 2036 compare posted reachable bill-covering jobs only if still employed and hours fell.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: How does it feel, picturing that?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would be uneasy about distant robots while both wages and our present reserve cover us. I want to make our last-shift decision with a pencil and the actual bills.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: If the figures fall short?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: I would continue safe paid work and compare posted wages after travel if shifts fell. I would not leave because a birthday came.

transcript.speaker: interviewer
transcript.text: Would the children support you?

transcript.speaker: persona
transcript.text: They have their own homes. We can discuss the plan, but I would not count their wages as ours.

I would separate **2036 AGI** from 2039 bottle robots.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Of the five pictures, which one worries you most, and what would actually help?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: AGI by 2028 worries me most because capable bottle robots around 2031 could close a shift including my lead post while the mortgage runs. Written staffing terms, offered funded paid safe training and posted reachable work with enough pay after travel would help.

closing.speaker: interviewer
closing.text: Is there anything I did not ask?

closing.speaker: persona
closing.text: Ask whether the first bottle holds a cap before a crate is wrapped. One chipped neck can undo a careful hour at the mould.

headlineQuote: One chipped neck can undo a careful hour at the mould.

He uses **AI occasionally** and would learn new defect alerts only in offered paid guarded supervised practice.
Expected **2031 shift closure** alarms him; a planned age-sixty-seven exit needs verified household income.
biggestWorry: **AGI by 2028** worries him most because 2031 bottle robots could close a shift including his lead post.
